para.dtcname: Brake Pedal Travel Is Excessive (No Fluid Leakage or Air in Lines)

test2.ptxt: Operate the brake pedal and inspect for mechanical malfunctions in pedal operation.
Inspect the brake pedal height, freeplay and reserve distance. (see )

atten4.ptxt: To identify the malfunctioning part, adjust the pedal height after completing each inspection.

test2.ptxt: Inspect that the disc brake pads of each wheel brake are installed correctly.
Inspect for loose bleeder plugs and union bolts, damaged gaskets, and fluid leakage from the wheel cylinders.

test1.ptxt: Inspect for Brake Fluid Leakage and Air Entry

test2.ptxt: Check the fluid level in the brake master cylinder reservoir.
Operate the brake pedal repeatedly and check that there is no abnormal feel (spongy feel from air) when operating the pedal.
Inspect for changes in the fluid level in the brake master cylinder reservoir.
If the fluid level decreases, inspect for fluid leakage due to damaged flexible hoses or brake tubes, loose union nuts, or a faulty master cylinder seal.
Bleed the air from the brake pipelines and actuator assembly. (see )

test1.ptxt: Depress the brake pedal while the brake pedal continues to sink.
Using the SST (TaSCAN), drive the ABS motor relay with the Active Test and inspect the change in pedal height when the pump motor rotates. (see )

specitem.ptxt: No change in brake pedal height (pedal remains sunk and does not return)

test1.ptxt: Inspect that there is no fluid leakage from the brake master cylinder and that the piston does not sink.
